title: Reverse the Playlist
story: A music app stores each playlist as a chain of songs. Every song knows only which song comes next; there is no way to jump back.
A listener taps "Play in reverse". The app must flip the chain in place, so every song points to the one that used to come before it.
task: Write reversePlaylist(head). head is the first node of a singly linked list (each node has val and next). Reverse the list and return the new first node.
An empty playlist is null (None in Python). Lists are shown as arrays like [3, 8, 1, 9]; your function receives and returns real nodes.
constraints: Reverse the links; do not just create a reversed copy of the values (though that also passes the tests, it misses the point).

examples.explanation: 3 → 8 → 1 → 9 with every arrow flipped is 9 → 1 → 8 → 3. The new head is 9.
An empty playlist stays empty. Return null (None in Python).

hints: Take 8 in 3 → 8 → 1 → 9. After reversing, where should its next point?
Each next must point to the node before it, but a node does not know its predecessor. You must carry that as you walk forward.
Keep prev (starting at null) for the node you just visited. Changing current.next loses your only way forward. What must you save first?
Walk with prev, current and next. Each step: save next = current.next, set current.next = prev, then prev = current, current = next. When current is null, prev is the new head.
bruteForce: Copy every value into an array, then build a new list from the array backwards.
That is O(n) time, but O(n) extra memory, and it skips the real skill: rewiring pointers without losing your place. The in-place version uses O(1) extra memory.

walkthrough: Flipping current.next destroys your only link to the rest of the list, so save it first.
1. prev = null, current = 3. Save next = 8. Point 3 → null. Now prev = 3, current = 8.
• Save next = null. Point 1 → 8. Now prev = 1, current = null.
The list reads 1 → 8 → 3 → null, and prev is its head. For an empty list the loop never runs and you return null.
solution.spaceWhy: Three pointer variables, whatever the list length.
solution.takeaway: When rewiring a linked list, save the pointer you are about to overwrite. The prev / current / next dance recurs in reversing part of a list, reordering, and palindrome checks.
